text.p: Singapore will ban smoking in almost all enclosed and air-conditioned areas starting August 15, a statement by the Ministry of Environment said on Saturday.
The measure was aimed at protecting non-smokers from second-hand smoke, the statement added.
Singapore currently prohibits smoking in selected areas including hospitals, cinemas, queues and certain air-conditioned restaurants and shops.

But from August 15, the ban will be extended to cover all air-conditioned shops, restaurants, private clubs, bowling alleys, barber shops, games arcades, libraries and all enclosed or air-conditioned areas in universities.
Smoking will also be banned at entire school compounds and other education centres.
Anyone caught smoking in a prohibited area is liable for a fine of S$1,000 (US$694.50).
Statistics from the Ministry of Environment estimate that 17 percent of Singapore's population are smokers.
